method: Reviewed existing Europe/North Atlantic and Asia/Middle East packets, checked their boundary and evidence dispositions, and recorded only the training role justified by the cited sources. Existing accepted packets are referenced rather than duplicated. A numerical population estimate is not promoted to a capacity target when it is a fiscal register, city/market estimate, trade-dependent urban total, or lacks an exact EU5 boundary.

records.reason: Existing wave3 packet has a real EU5 crosswalk and a conservative 2,224-person local-support floor. Mortensen's tax-land reconstruction supplies the population estimate; the 1298 Sheep Letter and modern historical synthesis document ecological carrying-capacity pressure and a predominantly sheep/barley/marine food regime. It is not promoted to a global saturation anchor because the sources do not identify a human-equilibrium ceiling.

The environmental carrying-capacity simulation and demographic reconstruction are useful hostile-island checks with a complete island crosswalk, but the reconstructed population and modeled envelope are not an independently documented Malthusian saturation interval. Keep fully held out.

The Human Ecology synthesis reports sustainable-population-model estimates of a small peak around AD 1300 (1,400–2,200 people), and independently documents livestock, hay, seal, caribou, seabird, and fish subsistence plus farm abandonment and increasing marine reliance. It does not provide a mappable human-equilibrium ceiling, and the Eastern/Western Settlement footprint is not yet an audited >=95% EU5 crosswalk. Use as a hostile local-food validation case, never as a two-sided target.

County population totals are mappable and document marginal cultivation/pressure, but no independent county-level saturation interval is established. England's national 1290–1315 packet remains the only scale anchor; using county totals as labels would turn observed population into a hidden target.

The French hearth assessment can support a cautious aggregate interval only after its local-food and boundary semantics are audited. Rural Flanders and Tuscany records are market-integrated and their proposed boundaries mix towns, ports, and hinterlands; they cannot identify intrinsic local capacity without a quantified import share and pressure interval. They remain excluded/held out.

Farris Table 1.3 provides area-weighted 1280 rice-kokudaka floors and a documented dry-field sensitivity; CHGIS polygons provide audited EU5 crosswalks. These are productive-land lower bounds, not direct population counts or saturation estimates, so they remain one-sided validation constraints.

The same Farris/CHGIS register is useful evidence, but the measured centroid or area coverage is below the >=95% contract for Bungo, Hyuga, Satsuma, Oosumi, and Hizen, while Wakasa has no dedicated EU5 boundary. The detailed rejection reasons and measured ratios are in asia_japan_register_dispositions_wave7.json; no name-only replacement is permitted.

The reviewed records provide settlement, fiscal, or irrigation-history evidence but lack at least one of: a mappable EU5 boundary with >=95% coverage, a local-food population interval for that same boundary, or independent saturation/pressure evidence. They remain blocked or validation-only; no national/regional extrapolation is allowed.
